#Convert varaibles. 

```{r as.factor}
factor_columns <- c("AREA.NAME", "DATE.OCC", "Crm.Cd.Desc", "Mocodes", 
                    "Status", "Status.Desc", "LOCATION", "Date.Rptd")
crime[factor_columns] <- lapply(crime[factor_columns], function(col) as.factor(as.character(col)))
```

#Identify Rows and Columns with 20% or more Missing values. 

``` {r ID missing columns and rows by 20 percent}
# 1. IDENTIFY ROWS WITH ≥ 20% MISSING VALUES
# Calculate percentage of missing values per row
row_missing_pct <- rowMeans(is.na(crime)) * 100

# Extract rows with 20% or more missing values
rows_with_20_missing <- crime[row_missing_pct >= 20, ]

# Print number of affected rows
cat("Number of rows with ≥ 20% missing values:", nrow(rows_with_20_missing), "\n")

# Display affected rows (optional)
print(rows_with_20_missing)

# 2. IDENTIFY COLUMNS WITH ≥ 20% MISSING VALUES
# Calculate percentage of missing values per column
col_missing_pct <- colMeans(is.na(crime)) * 100

# Extract column names with 20% or more missing values
cols_with_20_missing <- names(crime)[col_missing_pct >= 20]

# Print results
cat("Columns with ≥ 20% missing values:\n")
print(cols_with_20_missing)
```


# Handle missing data. 
``` {r Handle Missing Categorical values}
# 1. REMOVE ROWS WITH ≥ 20% MISSING VALUES
# Calculate the percentage of missing values per row
row_missing_pct <- rowMeans(is.na(crime)) * 100

# Keep only rows with < 20% missing values
crime_cleaned <- crime[row_missing_pct < 20, ]

# Print the number of rows removed
cat("Number of rows removed:", nrow(crime) - nrow(crime_cleaned), "\n")

# 2. REMOVE COLUMNS WITH ≥ 20% MISSING VALUES
# Calculate the percentage of missing values per column
col_missing_pct <- colMeans(is.na(crime_cleaned)) * 100

# Select columns where missing percentage is < 20%
crime_cleaned <- crime_cleaned[, col_missing_pct < 20]

# Print the number of columns removed
cat("Number of columns removed:", ncol(crime) - ncol(crime_cleaned), "\n")

```
#Imputation
Here is where the NAs of the data are changed to fit the rest of the dataset. 

```{r Imputation Graph}
# Check the distribution of numerical columns
num_cols <- crime_cleaned %>% select(where(is.numeric))


num_cols %>%
  gather() %>%
  ggplot(aes(value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "blue", alpha = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ key, scales = "free") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Numeric Variables",
       x = "Value",
       y = "Frequency")

```

.


```{r Imputation}

# Calculate Mean and Median for numeric columns
num_summary <- num_cols %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), list(mean = ~mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                                      median = ~median(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                                      missing_pct = ~mean(is.na(.x)) * 100)))
# IMPUTATION BASED ON DISTRIBUTION

crime_imputed <- crime_cleaned %>%
  mutate(
    Vict.Age = ifelse(is.na(Vict.Age), median(Vict.Age, na.rm = TRUE), Vict.Age),  # Using Median due to skewness
     TIME.OCC= ifelse(is.na(TIME.OCC), mean(TIME.OCC, na.rm = TRUE), TIME.OCC)  # Using Mean due to normality
  )

# Handle categorical missing values using Mode
mode_impute <- function(x) {
  ux <- unique(x[!is.na(x)])  # Get unique non-NA values
  ux[which.max(tabulate(match(x, ux)))]  # Get most frequent value (mode)
}

summary(crime_imputed)

```


# Verify Data Cleaning
```{r}

summary(lm(AREA ~ Status.Desc + Crm.Cd.Desc + LOCATION, data = crime_imputed))
```
